sources.subject: San Diego County Broadband NOFA Public Meetings
attachments: San Diego County Broadband Public Meeting Flyer.pdf
sources.body:
Hi Travis,

Hope this email finds you well! The County of San Diego's Land Use & Environment Group (LUEG) is conducting a series of public meetings from May 20 - June 4 to gather public feedback and input on an upcoming Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) on a $9 million ARPA-funded grant program to help address broadband access and affordability in unincorporated communities. This is a continuation of public engagement activities that helped inform the Comprehensive Broadband Plan<https://www.sandiegocounty.gov/lueg/broadband/> released January 2023. We are inviting Alpine Community Planning Group to participate in this process.

The County is seeking public input on the criteria and scoring for the grant awards that were recently released via a draft Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA)<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/broadband>. There are a couple ways your community members can provide their feedback:

  1.  Attending one of the scheduled in-person public meetings (meeting flyer attached) or virtual webinar (details forthcoming)
  2.  Submitting written comments directly through the County's broadband engagement website (https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/broadband) or by email (broadband.grants@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:broadband.grants@sdcounty.ca.gov>)

We kindly ask you to help circulate this information with your network. All public comments on the draft NOFA are due by June 10th.

The County has contracted Guidehouse, a management consulting firm, to assist in this effort. I have copied the Guidehouse team members; please reach out to Lucy O'Keeffe (lokeeffe@guidehouse.com<mailto:lokeeffe@guidehouse.com>) and Harrison Phelan (hphelan@guidehouse.com<mailto:hphelan@guidehouse.com>) with questions. Also copied on this email are Stephanie Johnson (Stephanie.Johnson@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Stephanie.Johnson@sdcounty.ca.gov>) and Michael De La Rosa (Michael.DeLaRosa@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:Michael.DeLaRosa@sdcounty.ca.gov>), the County contacts for this engagement.

Thank you for your support of this endeavor, and we hope to see you there.

Best,
Lucy

sources.subject: Re: We Still Need An Advocate.
sources.body:
Randy Moore

US Chief Forester

1400 Independence Ave. 

Washington DC 20250-0003

Dear Chief Moore,
The public in the region of Loveland Reservoir in the Cleveland National Forest are in great need of your  long-standing resolution to public service. 

I am writing to follow up on our recent local non-profit Friends of Loveland Reservoir to Forest Service contact regarding Sunrise to Sunset access and the compatibility of the easement-protected "shoreline"  fishing program with Sweetwater Authority's water licenses and California environmental and water regulations. 

As you will see from this 4 year old email chain, this is something I was pleading for your help with and trying to help the Forest Service understand as far back as September 2020.

It is clear from the easement, land swap origination documents, and past  Forest Service oversight of Loveland Reservoir that volunteers are not a factor in the public's right and need to access the hiking, fishing, and birdwatching program.  I don't agree with the pursuit of such a program of volunteers, or with exposing Loveland recreation users to the risk of failure of it and another lengthy setback on therapeutic recreation and subsistence fishing for lower-income earners in the region.

Sweetwater is simply obligated by the land swap and easement to provide access to the lake until sunset 365 days a year. Supervision during those hours, or lack thereof, is Sweetwater's business, not that of citizens, or the US Forest Service.  This is all 100% legally unambiguous. Please call out your legal department’s claims otherwise and/or have that analysis reviewed by another independent agency.

Fortunately, others in the community are stepping up. Please create a path for remedies to having lost much of Loveland's public benefits since our earlier failed communications and failure to implement the protection and remedies at Loveland that so many of us have petitioned Supervisor Tangenberg to act on for so many years now. 

Sincerely,

Russell Walsh

4639 Montiel Truck Trail

Jamul CA, 91935

619-922-6235

    On Friday, September 18, 2020 at 08:35:44 AM PDT, Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com> wrote:

  Mr. Tangenberg,

Thank you for that email. Why would you want to renew the agreement other than to weaken what is already a substantially good easement as far as hours of access if it were respected? What terms are being considered for renewal? The lake fishing program is small but in geographical terms relative to the overall size of the lake, and then when the Sweetwater Authority drains it to send water the their other reservoir downstream it becomes even smaller.

Now I hear from Sweetwater Authority board meetings that they are considering lowering the lake below emergency levels. Are you aware of what the means for the fishing program? I would like to know . I would like to know that you are watching out for us on these items and are willing to fight for the U.S public.

The Sweetwater Authority does not have an elected representative in the area or the Reservoir and they can not be made to give a damn about the people who use the lake other than in court and I just can't do that.

Thank you,

Russell Walsh
     On Friday, September 18, 2020, 07:39:23 AM PDT, Tangenberg, Scott R -FS <scott.tangenberg@usda.gov> wrote:

 Mr. Walsh,My understanding is that the Sweetwater Authority is continuing to consider ways in which they can safely administer their fishing program more than 3 days per week.  As I said in my last note, we will work with them to renew our agreement once our current emergencies reach some new level of resolution.
If you still feel compelled to contact my supervisor, his name is Randy Moore, Region 5 Regional Forester, and he can be reached at randy.moore@usda.gov.
Scott TangenbergForest Supervisor, Cleveland National Forestscott.tangenberg@usda.gov209-470-345910845 Rancho Bernardo RDSan Diego, CA 92127
From: Russell Walsh <russellwalsh2003@yahoo.com>
Sent: Monday, September 14, 2020 10:45:26 AM
To: Tangenberg, Scott R -FS <scott.tangenberg@usda.gov>
Subject: Re: Referals To Your Supervisor and To A 'Whistle Blower"Contact. Mr. Tangenberg ,

You give way too much credit on this issues to the Sweetwater Authority and way to little to me and the public you represent. Because of this you come across as a real kiss up kick down kind of guy, one with blinders on who can not or will not see that the Sweetwater Authority is scamming the public . You don't work for the politcal/business interests in the region first and the public second. You have it backwards. Sweetwater Authorty is the worst lake of many in our region on returning rights as social distancing has relaxed for recreation and as public health prerogatives by the leadership, other than you, in our broader communities have shifted toward enabling outdoor activity.

You are already to forgive the Sweetwater Authorities obligations on the basis of the Valley fire , for as long as they want that and the fire didn't even reach Loveland. I know because it ripped through my property and was contained before it got there. The lake can be operated 7 days a week sunrise to sunset , no problem. Please quit giving it away like some lackey for the Political and Business entity that the Sweetwater Authority is.

You told me that all those request I made went directly back to you. So, I have never had appropriate contact with any level above yours to deal with this issue. So, it is you job as an honorable personIt to tell your supervisors at the National and other Levels that I have lost faith in you and that I should have recourse above you. I certainly do not want to work with anyone under your authority. such as a Descanso ranger,

If the leadership in your organization approves of how you lied to me and played pawn to the Sweetwater Authority , we really do have traitors in the government. My feeling is no one has much knowledge of what is happening but you and I . That needs to change.

Please do what I asked.

Russell Walsh
On Monday, September 14, 2020, 10:20:37 AM PDT, Tangenberg, Scott R -FS <scott.tangenberg@usda.gov> wrote:

Mr. Walsh,
I've been as clear as I can be in my previous communications.  Sweetwater Authority has the jurisdiction on access to Loveland Reservoir.  While a public access easement exists, our partner knows best during these trying times how access can be facilitated.  The Cleveland National Forest (and every National Forest in California) is currently closed to public access given the extreme fire risk and dangerous fire conditions.  The Valley Fire burn area will be closed for some time in the future as well.

All that said, I've cc'd Bob Heiar, our District Ranger for the Descanso Ranger District, and the local manager for this part of the Forest.  He has expressed to me an interest in revisiting the expired agreement with Sweetwater Authority sometime in the future, in order to reaffirm that commitment and establish a good arrangement for continued access and opportunities for the public there.

As to your question about supervisor contact or whistle-blower reporting, you have already been in contact with both our National and Regional Offices, and your concerns have been referred to me. When conditions change, regarding COVID, fires, fire weather, and the extreme challenges managing through these, I will do everything I can to safely re-establish access for our public.

Scott Tangenberg

sources.subject: Feasibility Study Interview Request - California State Water Resources Control Board
sources.body:
Good afternoon,

My name is Marissa, with Katz & Associates, and I'm part of a team under the California State Water Resources Control Board that is studying the feasibility of consolidating properties with individual groundwater wells or independent water systems east of Alpine with the Padre Dam Municipal Water District.

I'm reaching out today to see if you're interested in participating in an interview that will inform a Feasibility Study.

Background
The California State Water Resources Control Board<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/> (Board) under the Safe and Affordable Funding for Equity and Resilience (Safer) Drinking Water Program<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/grants_loans/sustainable_water_solutions/safer.html>, is funding planning efforts, including a Feasibility Study (Study), to support communities and help ensure a safe and reliable water supply for the future.

Due to some water quality concerns of existing groundwater wells in the Willowside Terrace community, located just east of the city of Alpine, the Board is conducting a Study to determine if this community can be connected to the Padre Dam Municipal Water District<https://www.padredam.org/> (PDMWD) to ensure a high quality, reliable and sustainable water supply is available for the future.

The Study team is interested in forming an expanded study area to include additional properties near Willowside Terrace that also use an independent water system reliant on groundwater.

As the Alpine Community Planning Group, the Study team is interested in participating in an interview with you to gather insights into the communities east of Alpine, near the potential study area. The Study team is interested in a range of views, opinions and experiences about independent water systems, the services provided by PDMWD, and the possibility of consolidating independent water systems with the district

Please let me know if you are interested in participating in an interview and what your availability looks like for the next few weeks.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Marissa Twite (she/her/hers)
Account Supervisor

sources.body:
Hello Travis,
 
Here is an example of a ruhric for community selected trail improvements. It is just an example. I most recently asked Senator Jones' staff to allow for Barry Jantz. the facilitator for the Alpine meeting,  or another skilled person to create a rubric with public input before the Alpine Women's club meeting.  
You mentioned the problem of time to impliment such a rubric. However, we have been asking for this for months. A rubric along with a deadline for input, would have kept clear any appearances of favoritsm and jumping to the head of the line with social/ political status and/or alliance with the Sweetwater Board,  despite low input for and with Senator Jones' staff along the way. There would not be a risk of making irrelevant previous honest efforts at crowdsourcing ideas from actual lake users , organizing them, and presenting them. 
 I understand that you showed sensitivity to this on the phone and I appreciate it. Maybe there are long term benefits to ACPG showing a stake in Loveland  now. I encouraged it with you. However, This is why I am asking that ACPG continue to do some of the hard work too. Like get sunrise to sunset back on track. The Descanso Ranger's condition of volunteers has been debunked. I would be glad to walk you and your board members through that with the set of documents that I have.

request_text:
Re: Public Records Act Request

Dear Alpine Community Planning Group Members,

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I am writing to request a copy of the records detailed below.

I am researching how the Alpine Community Planning Group (ACPG) conducts its business on the part of the residents of Alpine in preparation for publication of an expose. To that end, I request the following records:

1. All Alpine Community Planning Group Agendas and Minutes from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025.

2. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another member(s) of the Alpine Community Planning Group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

3. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another government agency, including between the group members and the County of San Diego from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

4. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and any member of the public, including between the group members and individuals/entities with business before the group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

Please note that the Public Records Act allows a member of the public to request records by describing their content, rather than asking for specific documents by name; an agency that receives such a request must “search for records based on criteria set forth in the search request.”

Public records represent “any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, photocopying, transmitting by electronic mail or facsimile, and every other means of recording upon any tangible thing any form of communication or representation, including letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combinations thereof, and any record thereby created, regardless of the manner in which the record has been stored.” (Government Code section 7920.545.)

1. This request applies to all records in your agency’s possession, including documents created by a member of another government agency or a member of the public.

2. If specific portions of any documents are exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portions.

3. Please provide entire documents, even if only parts of them are responsive to this request.

If you maintain records or data in electronic format, please provide them in that same format.

1 California First Amendment Coalition v. Superior Court, 67 Cal.App.4th 159, 165-66 (1998).
2 See California State University v. Superior Court, 90 Cal. App. 4th 810, 824-25 (1999).
3 Gov’t. Code § 6253(a). versions are acceptable) to avoid copying costs.
4 If you are unable to reproduce electronic records in electronic form, please provide a reason for doing so.

I request that you waive copying fees because I have limited resources, and the information requested will be used in the public interest to further the public’s understanding of the local community planning group action. None of the information obtained will be sold or distributed for profit. If you are unable to waive the copying fees, and you anticipate that these costs will exceed $50, or that the time needed to copy the records will delay their release, please contact me so that we can arrange to inspect the document or decide which documents we wish to have copied. Otherwise, please copy and send them as soon as possible. Please respond to this request within ten (10) days, either by providing all the requested records or by providing a written response setting forth the legal authority for withholding or redacting any document and stating when the documents will be made available.

If you require any clarification in identifying responsive documents or focusing this request, please contact [redacted]. Please send all records responsive to this request to Louis Russo.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

[redacted]

Gov’t. Code § 6253.9.
Gov’t. Code §§ 6253(c), 6255.
Gov’t. Code § 6253.1.
